name: Calvren Bissap-Cardamom Reserve
description: A premium small-batch soda using real dried bissap flowers steeped in cold water and blended with green cardamom extract, lightly sparkling and bottled in 250ml dark glass. One of the few sodas that uses genuinely traditional preparation methods at scale.
flavor_profile: Deep, wine-like hibiscus tartness with floral cardamom warmth, a mild natural sweetness from cane sugar, and a long, complex aftertaste with faint rose and spice.
cultural_context: Calvren is the kind of product that appears on Tier 4 dining tables as a non-alcoholic option at formal meals. Its small production run and genuine preparation process give it credibility that most corporate botanical brands can't fake — though Calvren's investors would like to scale it, and that tension is internal and ongoing.
story_hooks: Calvren's head of production has quietly been diverting a small percentage of each batch to sell independently at a significantly higher price — and has been doing it for years.
A Tier 5 household has placed a standing order for Calvren that exceeds the company's entire monthly output; fulfilling it would require refusing all other customers.
The real bissap flowers in Calvren's supply chain come from a single licensed grower who has just died with no clear succession — the future of the product is suddenly uncertain.
